elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Both the retained 12.1.1 and the new 12.1.3 say only "will indemnify and hold ... harmless"; no defence obligation is imposed on SFJ. To meet this element the drafter must add "defend" (and control of the defence) to SFJ's obligation.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: 12.1.1 runs to "PB; its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, employees and agents (the 'PB Indemnified Parties')" for Third Party Claims, and new 12.1.3 uses the same "PB Indemnified Parties" definition.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: New 12.1.3 covers Claims alleging that SFJ's performance of its obligations "or any materials, technology or methods supplied by SFJ hereunder, infringes or misappropriates such Third Party's Intellectual Property".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: 12.1.1(a)-(f) as rendered covers gross negligence/wilful misconduct, breaches of the Agreement/Protocol and post-Program-Transfer trial and product liability; no limb addresses SFJ's breach of applicable law, and 12.1.3 is IP-only.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No limb of 12.1.1 or new 12.1.3 references unauthorised access to or disclosure of PB data caused by SFJ.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Retained 12.1.1(a): "the gross negligence or willful misconduct of SFJ or any of its Affiliates or any of its or their respective Permitted Third Parties in performing SFJ's obligations under this Agreement".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: 12.2.1 "Notice of Claim" requires prompt written notice (Indemnification Claim Notice), and the redline conforms the cross-reference to "Section 12.1.1, 12.1.2 or 12.1.3" so it captures the new indemnity.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Only 12.2.1 (notice) is rendered; the rationale asserts existing control-of-defence mechanics in Article 12.2 but no such text is before us to verify, and 12.1.3 itself grants no defence control.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: No cooperation provision appears in the rendered language; 12.2.1 only obliges the Indemnified Party to furnish copies of papers and official documents. Any cooperation covenant sits in unrendered Article 12.2 text.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: PB's indemnity at 12.1.2 still covers (d) PB's material breach of the Agreement, (e) Protocol breach, (f) IP infringement by the Product or by PB's performance, and (g) Subject injuries/Commercialization claims — far broader than Customer content plus breach of law.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Inserted 12.1.3: "SFJ will indemnify and hold the PB Indemnified Parties harmless from any and all Losses arising or resulting from any Claim by a Third Party alleging that the performance by SFJ ... or any materials, technology or methods supplied by SFJ hereunder, infringes or misappropriates such Third Party's Intellectual Property".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Exclusion (i): "modifications made by or for PB".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Exclusion (ii): "combination of the affected item with items not supplied by SFJ".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: "SFJ will procure for PB the right to continue using the affected item, or will modify or replace it so that it becomes non-infringing" — mandatory ("will"), triggered where an item "is or may become the subject of such a Claim".

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: "if none of the foregoing is commercially reasonable, SFJ will refund the amounts paid by PB to SFJ for the affected item." Remedy is present and mandatory; note the item-specific basis is imprecise in a co-development payment structure (see reasons).

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: "SFJ's aggregate liability under this Section 12.1.3 will not exceed three times the aggregate amounts paid or payable by PB to SFJ under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the Claim", with a floor of three times first-twelve-months amounts; both limbs are 3× an annual figure and the cap is scoped to 12.1.3 only.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: new Section 12.1.3 supplies the SFJ IP indemnity, the three customary exclusions (PB modifications, combinations with non-SFJ items, PB specifications), the procure/modify/replace ladder, the refund backstop, and a 3× annual-amounts super-cap scoped only to 12.1.3 so SFJ's existing uncapped indemnities are untouched.

Preferred is not complete: no express duty to defend, no breach-of-applicable-law or data-breach limbs, PB's indemnity at 12.1.2 remains far broader than Customer content plus breach of law, and control-of-defence/cooperation mechanics are not in the rendered text (cannot be verified).

Minimality holds. The narrowing of 12.1.2(f) from "either Party" to "PB" is not gratuitous: left unchanged it would require PB to indemnify SFJ for infringement caused by SFJ's own performance, directly circling back on and neutralising the new 12.1.3, and the rule's own redline guidance contemplates narrowing Customer's indemnity where the clause is one-sided. The 12.2.1 cross-reference edit is a necessary conforming change so notice mechanics reach 12.1.3.

The cap floor ("in no event less than three times the aggregate amounts payable by PB to SFJ ... in the first twelve (12) months in which such amounts become due") does not exceed the 3×-annual threshold in substance — it is the same multiple applied to a different annual period — and is necessary because PB's payments to SFJ are Approval-triggered, so a pure trailing-twelve-month cap would be zero (and the indemnity worthless) for most of the term.

Intent preserved: the loss/net-of-tax-benefit mechanics, the mutual gross-negligence/material-breach carve-outs in 12.1.1 and 12.1.2, and the notice regime survive without contradiction; no defined term is orphaned and the only cross-reference touched is conformed.

Drafting point to tighten (not a completeness failure): the refund is measured by "the amounts paid by PB to SFJ for the affected item", but PB's payments under this Agreement are Approval Payments rather than item-priced consideration. Consider "a pro-rata portion of the amounts paid by PB to SFJ attributable to the affected item, or if not separately attributable, the amounts paid in the preceding twelve (12) months" to avoid an indeterminate refund base.

If pushing for the preferred position, add (i) "defend" plus SFJ control of the defence to 12.1.1/12.1.3, (ii) limbs for SFJ's breach of applicable law and unauthorised access to or disclosure of PB data caused by SFJ, and (iii) a narrowing of 12.1.2 to PB-provided content and PB's breach of law.
